name: Man Buddha Temple
significance: A Theravada Buddhist temple at Sale in Myanmar's Magway Region that enshrines the Shinbin Maha Laba Man Buddha, a hollow gold-lacquered figure of about 20 feet said to be the largest lacquer Buddha image in the country. The image itself is dated to around 1300.
story: The image is said to have floated downriver from Monywa to Sale during the great floods of 1888.

name: Bút Tháp Temple
significance: A Buddhist temple beside the Đuống River dyke in Bắc Ninh province, founded in the 13th century but whose surviving architecture, sculpture and decoration all belong to the 17th century, when the Zen master Chuyet Chuyet made it famous. Its ten buildings run for about 100 metres and hold a celebrated thousand-armed, thousand-eyed Quan Âm alongside the Buddha triad, Manjushri and Samantabhadra.

name: Quán Sứ Pagoda
deity: The Buddha (front hall); Master Minh Không (rear hall)
significance: A 15th-century Buddhist pagoda on Quan Su Street in central Hanoi, raised on the grounds of a Lê-dynasty guest house built for envoys from Champa and Laos, who as Buddhists wanted a place of worship on the premises. Renovated in 1822, it now serves as the headquarters of the Buddhist Sangha of Vietnam.

name: Changangkha Lhakhang
significance: One of Thimphu's oldest temples, set on a ridge above the city and founded in the 13th or 14th century by Nyima, a son of Phajo Drugom Zhigpo who brought the Drukpa Kagyu teachings to Bhutan. Its bronze Avalokiteshvara is the main image, and the protector Genyen Domtsangpa is invoked as the birth deity of children born at the national referral hospital below.
story: Some hold that the bronze Avalokiteshvara arose of itself rather than being carved, while others credit a Newar master craftsman working at the time the temple was built.

name: Kwan Im Thong Hood Cho Temple
deity: Guanyin (Kuan Yim), worshipped here in her Cundi form
significance: A Chinese Buddhist temple on Waterloo Street in Singapore's Rochor district, begun in 1884 after the firm Chen Liang Cheng gave the land, and rebuilt in 1895 and again in 1980. Its image of Cundi, a form of Guanyin, draws crowds of worshippers seeking good fortune.

name: Payathonzu Temple
significance: A late 13th-century brick temple at Minnanthu, southeast of Bagan, whose Burmese name means Temple of Three Buddhas: three shrines joined by narrow passages, left unfinished by its builders. Its interior murals are noted for Mahayana and Tantric elements unusual in Bagan.

name: Shwesandaw Pagoda
significance: The tallest pagoda at Bagan, raised in 1057 by King Anawrahta to enshrine hair relics of the Buddha brought from Thaton. Five receding terraces, once faced with terracotta Jataka plaques, carry a cylindrical stupa whose jewelled hti was thrown down by the earthquake of 1975.
